title: Peer Accounting Comparability and Focal Firms’ Earnings Management: A Perspective of Accounting Discretion
summary: This study investigates how firms manage earnings through accounting discretion when industry peers produce more comparable accounting information. Utilizing data from Chinese A‐share listed firms, we find that peer accounting comparability inhibits focal firms’ accruals‐based earnings management. We identify two possible mechanisms underlying this phenomenon. First, peer accounting comparability helps to establish generally accepted accounting practices that induce focal firms to align. Second, peer accounting comparability contributes to mitigating outsiders’ information asymmetry, thus improving external monitoring. Cross‐sectional analysis indicates that the effect of peer accounting comparability holds across varying levels of focal firms’ internal and external governance mechanisms. Furthermore, we find that manipulating accruals when peer accounting comparability is high causes lower cumulative abnormal returns during the earnings announcement window and a higher cost of equity. Finally, we show that when focal firms cannot manage earnings through accounting discretion because of high peer accounting comparability, they turn to real earnings management.

title: Digital transformation, supply chain integration, and supply chain performance: A bibliometric analysis of Scopus research trends (2016–2025)
summary: This study maps the development of research on the relationship between digital transformation, supply chain integration, and supply chain performance. It responds to the need for a focused bibliometric account of how digital technologies are positioned within supply chain management research beyond broad reviews of the field. A Scopus export dated 3 June 2026 was analysed, comprising 188 English-language records published between 2016 and 2025, including 174 articles and 14 reviews. Records were identified through a structured search strategy and analysed using descriptive bibliometric techniques, citation analysis, author productivity analysis, country analysis, and keyword normalisation. The results show substantial growth in publication activity, rising from 1 record in 2016 to 74 records in 2025. However, the most recent publication year should be interpreted with caution because database coverage remains sensitive to indexing and update cycles. The corpus accumulated 8562 Scopus citations, with a mean of 45.5 citations per record and a median of 19.5 citations per record. Sustainability (Switzerland), International Journal of Production Economics, Journal of Enterprise Information Management, Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review, and Supply Chain Management emerged as the most visible publication outlets. Normalised keyword patterns indicate that supply chain integration, supply chain performance, digital transformation, supply chain resilience, blockchain, collaboration, Industry 4.0, visibility and the Internet of Things constitute the dominant vocabulary of the field. The study contributes by showing that contemporary scholarship increasingly conceptualises supply chain performance as dependent on digitally enabled integration, visibility, collaboration, and organisational coordination capabilities.

title: THE EFFECT OF ACCOUNTING CONSERVATISM AND CORPORATE SOCIAL RESPONSIBILITY (CSR) DISCLOSURE ON EARNINGS MANAGEMENT: EMPIRICAL EVIDENCE FROM CONSUMER GOODS INDUSTRY COMPANIES LISTED ON THE DURING 2022–2025
summary: This study examines the effects of accounting conservatism and Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) disclosure on earnings management in consumer goods industry companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during the 2022–2025 period. Earnings management remains a major concern because it can reduce the reliability of financial reporting and create information asymmetry between management and stakeholders. This study employed a quantitative approach with a causal explanatory design using panel data regression analysis. The sample consisted of 44 consumer goods companies selected through purposive sampling, resulting in 176 firm-year observations. Earnings management was measured using discretionary accruals based on the Modified Jones Model, accounting conservatism was measured using the Conservative Accruals (CONACC) model, and CSR disclosure was measured using the Corporate Social Responsibility Disclosure Index (CSRDI). The results indicate that accounting conservatism has a positive and significant effect on earnings management, while CSR disclosure has a negative and significant effect on earnings management. Furthermore, accounting conservatism and CSR disclosure simultaneously have a significant effect on earnings management. These findings suggest that CSR disclosure contributes to reducing opportunistic reporting behavior, whereas accounting conservatism may provide managerial discretion that influences reported earnings.

title: ENVIRONMENTAL, SOCIAL, AND GOVERNANCE (ESG) PERFORMANCE AND EARNINGS MANAGEMENT: THE ROLE OF AUDIT QUALITY
summary: Grounded in Agency and Stakeholder theories, this research explores the influence of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) performance on earnings management, while also assessing whether audit quality serves as a moderating factor. The magnitude of earnings manipulation is evaluated using discretionary accruals. By applying a purposive sampling technique, the study analyzes 238 firm-year observations from non-financial corporations registered on the Indonesia Stock Exchange between 2020 and 2024. The data is processed utilizing Moderated Regression Analysis (MRA). The empirical outcomes reveal that organizations demonstrating superior ESG achievements are less likely to engage in earnings management. Conversely, audit quality, measured by the presence of a Big Four auditor, fails to show a significant moderating effect in reinforcing the linkage between ESG practices and reduced earnings manipulation. Keywords : Earnings Management, ESG, Audit Quality.

title: Aligning Corporate Governance with ILO Labor Standards: Challenges and Opportunities for Multinational Enterprises
summary: Multinational enterprises increasingly recognize the importance of aligning corporate governance frameworks with International Labor Organization requirements, but scholarship on this intersection remains limited. This paper addresses that gap by synthesizing evidence that improved governance mechanisms notably enhance labor compliance throughout international operations. The International Labor Organization establishes foundational requirements for respectable work—encompassing freedom of association, collective bargaining, non-discrimination, and workplace safety—that multinational firms have to operationalize through corporate decision-making systems and supply chain governance. Contemporary multinational businesses navigate competing pressures from regulators, shareholders, and civil society while managing labor-related human rights obligations across jurisdictions. Stakeholder-centric governance frameworks provide promising pathways for forums to institutionalize labor issues within operational workflows. Evidence demonstrates that active board oversight, strong due diligence mechanisms, and independent verification structures significantly improve compliance outcomes compared to voluntary codes alone. Leading multinationals in electronics, clothing, and extractive industries have correctly incorporated ILO-aligned measures into center governance systems, promoting both compliance and stakeholder engagement. However, effective implementation remains constrained by functional governance potential gaps in host nations and chronic deficiencies in corporate disclosure verification. This paper argues that integrating ILO standards into company governance constitutes both a strategic imperative for operational resilience and a mechanism for advancing sustainable development. Recommendations emphasize bolstered board duty, comprehensive supply chain due diligence, and unbiased outside verification regimes.

title: Examining the Impact of Corporate Information Communication Technology Resources on the Corporate Social Responsibility Performance of Tokyo‐Listed Firms
summary: ABSTRACT Corporate Information Communication Technology (ICT) assets play a vital role in improving corporate social responsibility (CSR) outcomes. They help with data management, increase transparency, and support effective communication with stakeholders. These abilities allow companies to better monitor, record, and implement socially and environmentally responsible actions. This research, based on the Resource‐Based View, investigates how corporate ICT assets influence CSR performance. It also examines whether firm size and innovation orientation influence this relationship. The study employed specific inclusion and exclusion criteria and utilized a purposive sampling method to select suitable firms. Data were collected from 483 non‐financial corporations of Tokyo‐listed firms between 2008 and 2024. Researchers gathered this information from the Bloomberg database. To confirm the reliability and strength of the findings, advanced second‐generation estimation methods were used. These included the Augmented Mean Group (AMG), the Common Correlated Effects Mean Group (CCEMG), and the two‐step Generalized Method of Moments (GMM). The findings indicate that investments in ICT, the intensity of ICT use, and ICT‐related research and development, as indicators of corporate ICT resources, have a positive impact on CSR performance. Additionally, interactions between ICT investment, firm size, and innovation orientation had significant positive effects on CSR outcomes. This highlights the need for corporate leaders to focus on building ICT infrastructure as part of their CSR and sustainability strategies, especially regarding CSR reporting and stakeholder engagement. The study also emphasizes the importance of policymakers in promoting digital transformation to enhance responsible corporate governance.

title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN AUDITING AND ACCOUNTING: A BIBLIOMETRIC ANALYSIS
summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is addressed in accounting and auditing research in relation to financial reporting, assurance services, fraud detection, risk management, and professional decision-making processes. This study combines data source-sensitive bibliometric profiling with VOSviewer-based text network analysis. Records, citations, annual citations, author-focused metrics, and the Age-Weighted Citation Rate accessed via Publish or Perish from Google Scholar, CrossRef, OpenAlex, Scopus, and Semantic Scholar data sources were compared. The findings indicate that bibliometric indicators vary depending on the data source, and that Scopus text networks offer a narrower, source-specific view of the core themes represented in the accessed records.

title: PENGARUH CORPORATE GOVERNANCE TERHADAP TAX AVOIDANCE
summary: This study aims to examine the effect of corporate governance on tax avoidance in manufacturing companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) during the 2022–2024 period. The corporate governance variables analyzed in this study include board independence, board gender diversity, board size, audit quality, and CEO narcissism, as well as financial characteristic variables, namely profitability and leverage. Tax avoidance is measured using the effective tax rate (ETR). This study employs a quantitative approach with a causal research design. The research sample was selected using a purposive sampling method, and secondary data were obtained from companies’ annual reports and financial statements. The data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, data quality tests, classical assumption tests, and hypothesis testing through multiple linear regression analysis. The results indicate that board independence, board gender diversity, board size, and audit quality do not have a significant effect on tax avoidance. Furthermore, CEO narcissism and leverage have a positive and significant effect on tax avoidance. Meanwhile, profitability has a negative and significant effect on tax avoidance.

title: Pengaruh Financial Distress dan Leverage terhadap Earnings Management dengan ESG Disclosure sebagai Variabel Moderasi
summary: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menguji pengaruh financial distress dan leverage terhadap manajemen laba serta menganalisis peran moderasi pengungkapan Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG). Penelitian dilakukan pada perusahaan sektor Consumer Non-Cyclicals yang terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia (BEI) selama periode 2019–2024. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan teknik purposive sampling dan memperoleh 262 observasi firm-year dari 105 perusahaan yang memenuhi kriteria penelitian. Manajemen laba diukur menggunakan discretionary accruals berdasarkan Modified Jones Model, financial distress diukur menggunakan Altman Z-Score, leverage diproksikan dengan Debt to Equity Ratio (DER), sedangkan pengungkapan ESG diukur menggunakan ESG Disclosure Index (ESGDI). Data dianalisis menggunakan regresi linear berganda dan Moderated Regression Analysis (MRA) dengan bantuan SPSS. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa financial distress tidak berpengaruh signifikan terhadap manajemen laba, dan leverage juga tidak berpengaruh signifikan terhadap manajemen laba. Selain itu, pengungkapan ESG tidak terbukti memoderasi hubungan antara financial distress dan manajemen laba. Namun, pengungkapan ESG terbukti memoderasi secara signifikan hubungan antara leverage dan manajemen laba, yang menunjukkan bahwa pengungkapan ESG dapat mengubah kekuatan pengaruh leverage terhadap manajemen laba. Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa tekanan keuangan tidak selalu mendorong perusahaan untuk melakukan manajemen laba, sedangkan pengungkapan ESG berperan dalam membentuk perilaku manajerial, khususnya pada kondisi perusahaan dengan tingkat leverage yang tinggi.

title: Green Supply Chain Finance and Systemic Risks in the Global South's Green Transition: An Approach Towards SDG 9
summary: ABSTRACT This study examines how green supply chain finance relates to systemic risks, including competitiveness risk, financial instability risk, and green transition‐related geopolitical exposure, across 15 Global South economies from 2014 to 2024. Extending prior firm‐level research, this study conceptualizes green supply chain finance as a macro‐level financial mechanism linking industrial transformation to systemic stability. A composite index of green supply chain finance is constructed using green financing and policy indicators, and panel fixed‐effects models are complemented by heteroskedasticity‐based instrumental variable estimation to address endogeneity. The results show that green supply chain finance is consistently associated with lower competitiveness risks and exhibits weaker but generally negative associations with financial instability and transition‐related external risks. Overall, the findings extend the green finance literature by providing cross‐country evidence on the relationship between green supply chain finance and systemic resilience, with implications for sustainable industrial development and the broader objectives of Sustainable Development Goal 9.

title: Insights Into the Roles of the Corporate Governance Mechanism in Sustainability Assurance Practices
summary: ABSTRACT Our study explores the roles of corporate governance mechanisms in sustainability assurance practices in China through 40 semi‐structured interviews with sustainability reporting preparers and assurance providers. Guided by framing theory, the findings unveil distinct frames of the two groups perceiving governance of sustainability assurance. Six influential governance mechanisms emerge, including boards of directors, audit committees, internal auditors, the Communist Party Committee, governing bodies and external assurance providers. Three insights are identified from the interviewees' storylines: (1) the Chinese central government and its authority departments dominate the sustainability assurance legitimacy process, (2) in the absence of comprehensive assurance standards, legitimacy needs to be maintained to constrain managerial opportunism and (3) organisational and regional cultural factors shape report preparers' and assurance providers' perceptions of sustainability activities. Our study extends the application of framing theory by providing preliminary evidence of legitimised corporate governance roles in an emerging economy context.

title: PENGARUH CORPORATE GOVERNANCE, FINANCIAL RATIO, AND OTHER FACTORS TERHADAP FIRM VALUE
summary: This study aims to analyze the effect of profitability, firm size, total asset growth, liquidity, leverage, total asset turnover, and audit committee structure on firm value. The population consists of manufacturing sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) during the 2020–2024 period, with 79 firms selected as samples using purposive sampling. Hypothesis testing was conducted using multiple linear regression analysis. The results show that profitability has a positive effect on firm value, as a higher ability to generate profits attracts investor interest. Total asset growth has a negative effect on firm value, indicating that asset growth without improvements in profitability and business sustainability is less attractive to investors. Leverage has a positive effect on firm value, reflecting the company’s ability to manage debt optimally. Meanwhile, total asset turnover has a negative effect on firm value, as high asset turnover does not represent an overall improvement in company performance. Firm size, liquidity, and audit committee structure have no effect on firm value.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Digital Transformation in Financial Services: Emerging Business Models, Opportunities and Challenges
summary: ABSTRACT The rapid development of Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML), cloud computing, big data analytics, blockchain and digital payment technologies is transforming the structure and functioning of modern commerce. The financial services sector is one of the most technology-intensive sectors, where digital transformation has changed traditional banking, payment systems, lending, investment management, insurance and customer relationship management. Artificial Intelligence has emerged as a particularly important technology because of its ability to analyse large volumes of structured and unstructured data, identify patterns, automate decisions and provide personalised services.This chapter examines the role of Artificial Intelligence in transforming financial services and creating emerging business models. It discusses major applications of AI in banking and finance, including fraud detection, credit assessment, customer service, personalised financial products, risk management, regulatory compliance, investment management and digital payments. The chapter also examines emerging models such as AI-powered banking, embedded finance, Banking-as-a-Service, FinTech platforms, intelligent digital lending and AI-enabled financial ecosystems. At the same time, the adoption of AI introduces challenges related to data privacy, cybersecurity, algorithmic bias, explainability, model risk, technological dependency and regulatory compliance. The chapter proposes a responsible AI adoption framework based on governance, data quality, transparency, human oversight, cybersecurity and continuous monitoring. The discussion is particularly relevant to emerging markets such as India, where digital public infrastructure and FinTech innovation are rapidly changing the financial ecosystem.

title: Regulatory Extraterritoriality in EU ESG Governance
summary: This article explores how the European Union’s Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) regulatory framework is creating de facto global standards that reach well beyond Europe’s borders. It argues that EU ESG rules represent a significant evolution of the classic ‘Brussels Effect’, extending the EU’s regulatory influence from traditional product standards to the way companies govern themselves, organize their operations, and manage their global value chains. Through landmark instruments the EU is actively shaping corporate behaviour around the world. The article identifies four key mechanisms driving this global diffusion: market access pressure, supply chain governance, financial market alignment, and normative legitimacy. In doing so, it conceptualizes this phenomenon as a new form of conduct-based extraterritoriality, in which EU rules increasingly influence not only what companies produce, but how they operate internally and across borders. At the same time, the article acknowledges important limitations, including growing regulatory fragmentation, high compliance costs (particularly for firms in developing countries), and rising geopolitical contestation. Ultimately, EU ESG regulation emerges as a powerful yet increasingly contested force in the transformation of global governance.

title: AI-Driven Self-Healing Supply Chains and the Future of Logistics Automation
summary: This study examines how artificial intelligence (AI) enables self-healing capabilities in global supply chains and reshapes logistics automation. Employing a qualitative multi-case study design, data were collected through 42 semi-structured interviews across six multinational organisations in manufacturing, retail, and third-party logistics. Thematic analysis yielded four themes: AI-enabled disruption sensing; autonomous reconfiguration mechanisms; human-AI collaboration and workforce transformation; and ethical and governance considerations. Findings demonstrate that self-healing capability emerges from the dynamic interplay between AI infrastructure, adaptive organisational routines, and human agency - not from technology alone. Organisations embedding AI within a dynamic capabilities’ framework achieve measurable reductions in disruption recovery time and operational costs. A grounded theoretical model of AI-driven supply chain self-healing is proposed, integrating dynamic capabilities theory and complex adaptive systems theory. Practical implications for supply chain leaders and directions for future mixed-methods research are discussed.

title: Labor Mobility in the Context of Globalization and the Digital Economy
summary: The article analyzes the transformation of labor mobility under the impact of the digital economy. The study aims to substantiate that digitalization replaces the physical relocation of workers with their virtual integration into employers' processes, and to assess whether the current level of digitalization in Russia is sufficient for full-scale labor mobility by 2028. The empirical basis comprises data from the statistical compendium "Digital Economy Indicators: 2026" (HSE University / Rosstat). The findings reveal that remote and platform-based employment cover 1.7% and 3.8% of the workforce respectively, with the highest intensity of remote work recorded in the IT industry (23.4%). Three systemic barriers are identified: a skills deficit (only 10.6% of the population possess basic or higher digital skills, while 75.4% lack information security competencies), infrastructural constraints (corporate VPN usage stands at merely 35.8% of organizations), and scale limitations (the ICT sector contributes 4.0% to GVA, equivalent to 3.9% of GDP, versus 7–9% in leading countries). The theoretical contribution lies in conceptualizing two divergent trajectories of digital mobility: genuine virtual integration and algorithmically mediated local employment. The study concludes that the current level of digitalization is insufficient for systemic labor market virtualization by 2028, a qualitative shift is realistically achievable no earlier than 2030–2032.

AI.abstract_translation: 本文分析了数字经济冲击下劳动力流动的转型。该研究旨在论证数字化以劳动者虚拟融入雇主流程的方式取代了劳动者的实体迁移，并评估俄罗斯当前的数字化水平是否足以在2028年前实现全面规模的劳动力流动。实证基础包括来自统计汇编《数字经济指标：2026》（HSE大学/俄罗斯联邦国家统计局）的数据。研究发现显示，远程就业与平台型就业分别覆盖了1.7%和3.8%的劳动力，远程工作强度最高的是IT行业（23.4%）。研究识别出三项系统性障碍：技能缺口（仅有10.6%的人口具备基础或更高水平的数字技能，而75.4%的人口缺乏信息安全能力）、基础设施约束（企业VPN使用率仅为35.8%的组织），以及规模限制（ICT部门对总增加值的贡献为4.0%，相当于GDP的3.9%，而领先国家为7–9%）。理论贡献在于概念化了数字流动性的两条分化路径：真正的虚拟融入与算法中介的本地就业。研究结论认为，当前数字化水平不足以在2028年前实现系统性的劳动力市场虚拟化，质的转变最早可实际实现的时间不早于2030—2032年。

title: CORPORATE GOVERNANCE DAN FAKTOR LAINNYA YANG MEMENGARUHI PENGHINDARAN PAJAK
summary: Tax avoidance is a strategy used by companies to reduce tax obligations by exploiting loopholes in tax regulations legally. This study aims to obtain empirical evidence on the effect of independent board of commissioners, board size of directors, board gender diversity, institutional ownership, managerial ownership, and leverage as independent variables on tax avoidance as the dependent variable. The research objects are manufacturing companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during the 2022–2024 period. The sample was selected using a purposive sampling method, resulting in 145 companies with a total of 435 observations. Data were analyzed using multiple linear regression with software IBM Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS) version 25. The results of this search indicate that independent board of commissioners, board size of directors, board gender diversity, institutional ownership, managerial ownership, and leverage have no effect on tax avoidance.

title: Cross-industry Technological Information Spillovers through Analyst Networks
summary: Do equity analysts transmit technological information across industries? I show that, through within-brokerage networks, analysts acquire technological knowledge from firms in other industries and apply it to the firms they cover. I measure these spillovers using technological connectedness (TC), based on patent-distribution similarity between a focal firm and firms covered by colleagues in other industries. Using brokerage M&As as quasi-exogenous shocks to analyst networks, I show that higher-TC analysts issue more accurate earnings forecasts. At the firm level, high-TC analysts improve innovation quality by curbing low-impact patenting. Coverage by high-TC analysts also attenuates technology momentum in stock returns.

title: Digital Transformation of Indian Commerce and the Changing World of Work: A Conceptual Review of Business, Employment and Workforce Capability
summary: This conceptual review examines how digital transformation is reshaping Indian commerce and the world of work that sustains it. Adopting an integrative literature review design, the study synthesises 30 scholarly and institutional sources, comprising foundational theory on technology and organisations, recent evidence on automation and artificial intelligence, and India-focused research and official reports on digitalisation, employment, informality and leadership, through thematic analysis. Four themes emerge: the digitalisation of commercial activity, the recomposition of employment, the centrality of workforce capability and leadership, and the risk of a widening divide between the organised economy and traditional and unorganised sectors. Official estimates place India's digital economy at 11.74% of national income in 2022-23, with a projected share of nearly one-fifth by 2029-30, which underlines the scale of the shift. The synthesis indicates that the employment effects of digitalisation are compositional and not uniformly negative, that returns to digital investment depend on complementary human and organisational capabilities, and that the informal workforce, including handloom producers, construction labour and migrant workers, remains largely outside the digital dividend. The paper integrates these insights into a Digital Commerce–Work–Capability framework and advances five research propositions for empirical testing. It offers practical guidance for business managers, educational institutions and policymakers seeking inclusive digital growth.
